title: Arabidopsis thylakoid domains proteome
projectDescription: The thylakoid membrane in land plants is organized into an appressed domain (grana), enriched in photosystem (PS) II, and a non-appressed domain (stroma lamellae) enriched in PSI. This ultrastructure ensures control over excitons spillover from PSII to PSI. The bulky machinery required for the repair and biogenesis of PSII and other proteins of the stacked, appressed domain is located in the non-appressed membranes. Thus, the connecting domain (CD) between grana and stroma lamellae, also known as the grana margins (GM), is the key player in both the structural and functional integrity of the photosynthetic machinery.  To elucidate the properties and composition of the GM proteome, we have analyzed the different thylakoid domains isolated from membranes in native conformation as well as from thylakoids artificially unstacked to induce a homogeneous protein composition. We show that the composition of the CD is strictly distinct from that of the highly curved structures (the curvature) present at the periphery of grana discs, which are not physically connected to the stroma lamellae. Furthermore, a detailed map of the composition, distribution and interaction of the protein complexes involved in thylakoid membrane function is provided for the grana, CD, curvature and stroma lamellae domains.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Plant growth, thylakoid isolation and fractionation To understand how the solubilization with digitonin (DIG) affects the distribution of the thylakoid protein complexes in fractions collected at increasing centrifugation speed, the following experimental procedure has been set up. Plants of wild-type Arabidopsis (Arabidopsis thaliana) ecotype Col-0 were grown under 120 µmol phot m-2s-1 (8 h light/16 h dark) using OSRAM PowerStar (Munich, Germany) HQIT 400/D Metal Halide lamps as the light source, for 32 days. Thylakoid membranes were isolated in dim light and at 4°C two hours after the onset of the light period from fresh whole rosettes ground in ice-cold buffer containing 50 mM Tricine/NaOH (pH 7.8), 400 mM sorbitol, 10 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, 10 mM NaF. After filtration through two layers of Miracloth, thylakoids were pelleted at 2739 x g at 4°C for 5 min, re-suspended in a shock buffer [15 mM Tricine/NaOH (pH 7.8), 10 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, 10 mM NaF] and centrifuged again at 630 x g at 4°C for 5 min. Thylakoids were washed with resuspension buffer [15 mM Tricine/KOH (pH 7.8), 100 mM sorbitol, 10 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, 10 mM NaF], centrifuged at 630 x g and finally re-suspended in the same buffer = resuspension buffer.  Next, thylakoid membranes were washed 6 times in either presence (washed) or absence (linearized) of MgCl2. The two preparations were subjected to solubilization with [DIG] corresponding to 0.1% w/v (0.8 mM), 0.25% (2 mM) or 0.4% (3.2 mM), as described in Trotta et al., 2019. A strong pellet was collected after centrifugation at 1,000 x g (unsolubilized material pellet, named UP or 1k), 10,000 x g (grana, G or 10k), 40,000 x g (grana margins, M or 40k) and 144,000 x g (stroma thylakoids or stroma lamellae, SL or 144k). Besides the strong pellets, a loose pellet (LP) was visible in all fractions (Supplemental Figure 1), and it was collected always at 144,000 g and, when indicated, at 40,000 x g (Figure 1A, see below). The LP at 144,000 x g, when needed, was further centrifuged as strong pellet at 178,000 x g. The chlorophyll (chl) content was measured according to (Porra et al., 1989). For analysis in mass spectrometry (MS) of intact thylakoid membranes and fractions proteomes, proteins equivalent to 5 µg of chlorophyll were loaded onto an SDS-PAGE gel containing 6 % acrylamide and 6 M urea 6%, run approximately 0.5 cm and excised for MS analysis. The excised gel pieces (~ 1 mm3) were shrunk completely by incubating 3 times for 10 min in 100 µl of 100% acetonitrile (ACN), incubated in 25 mM Dithiothreitol (DTT)/100 mM NH4HCO3 for 30 min at 56°C in a Thermomixer (Eppendorf) and, after shrinking as above, alkylated for 20 min with 55 mM of iodacetamide (IAA)/ 100 mM NH4HCO3 at 22°C in the dark. After two consecutive washes alternating 100% ACN and 100 mM NH4HCO3, the gel pieces were completely shrunk as described above. For protein digestion, the gel pieces were completely re-hydrated in a solution of 40 mM NH4HCO3/10% ACN with either 0.13 µg/µl (150 µl for total soluble proteins) of trypsin (Sequencing Grade Modified Trypsin V5111, Promega, Madison) at 4°C. After adding 20 µl of 40 mM NH4HCO3/10% ACN, the gel pieces were incubated at 37°C in the Thermomixer (Eppendorf) shaking at 600 rpm for 13-14 hours. The tryptic peptides have been extracted by an equal volume of 100% ACN  and incubating for 15 min at 37°C. The supernatant has been collected in a new Eppendorf and the gel pieces have been incubated two more times for 15 min with 50% ACN/5% formic acid (FA) to collect the remaining peptides. The supernatants have been pooled and dried in a speed-vac for 3 hours, and dissolved in 2% FA to be analyzed by nLC-ESI MS/MS. For mass spectrometry analysis, the peptides samples were separated on a C18 precolumn (5 × 0.3 mm, PepMap C18, LC Packings) and a C18 nanocolumn (15 cm × 75 μm, Magic 5 μm, 200 Å C18, Michrom BioResources, Sacramento, CA) with a flow rate of 300 nL/min using 0.1% FA, 2% ACN as a buffer A and 0.1% FA, 80% ACN as a buffer B. Gradients comprised 3 % to 43 % solvent B over 60 min (, followed by 43 % to 100 % solvent B for 5 min, and finally 100 % solvent B for 10 min. The mass spectrometer used was a Q-Exactive HF (Thermo Fisher Scientific), with resolution set to 120000, scan range 300 to 1800 m/z for MS1, and 15000 with scan range 200 to 2000 m/z for MS2. Dynamic exclusion was set to 30 s and up to 15 masses with m/z ≥2+ were selected for MS2 for every MS1 scan.
dataProcessingProtocol: The obtained MS/MS spectra have been analyzed via Mascot (v.2.6.1) and Sequest HT using Proteome Discover 2.4.0.305 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and the embedded ptmRS algorithm to validate the identified modifications. The variable modifications allowed were the followings: Met oxidation, protein N-term acetylation, Ser, Thr and Tyr phosphorylation. As fixed modificationC ys carbamidomethylation was set. The MS/MS spectra were matched against a non-redundant Arabidopsis proteome database (TAIR10; https://www.arabidopsis.org/) supplemented with most common contaminants (35,502 entries in total). False discovery rate of the identified peptides was evaluated using the Percolator node (v. 3.01.1) with the following settings:  Target/Decoy Selection:  Concatenated; Validation based on:  q-Value; FDR Targets:- Target FDR (Strict):  0.01 - Target FDR (Relaxed):  0.05. Posterior error probabilities was evaluated accordingly with the following Peptide Validator processing node setting: Validation Mode:  Automatic (Control peptide level error rate if possible).  For protein quantification, the following parameters were set in the Precurson Ions Quantifier node (Proteome Discover 2.4.0.305). Peptides to use: unique + razor. Precursor abundance based on: Area. Minimum number of replicates: 67%. Normalization mode: total peptide amount. Scaling mode: On controls average. Protein adundance calculated as: Summed abundances. Protein ratio calculation: protein abundance based. Maximum allowed fold change: 100. Imputation mode: low abundance resampling. Hypothesis test: ANOVA (Individual proteins). For grouping and quantification, the intact starting material (intact thylakoids) was set as control and the protein abundances in the fractions calculated relative to control (n=3).
